title: Marguerite and the Crown
premise: Felix Crane's forbidden gift for hearing beasts has kept him useful and expendable in the Ledgerhouse, a guild that trades in impossible things. When a feral child named Marguerite arrives speaking a language that predates every kingdom, Felix discovers she is the last living heir of the Old Covenant between the human realm and the wild — a pact the guild itself quietly broke a generation ago to seize its power. Hunted by the guild's enforcers and guided by the beasts he was never supposed to hear, Felix must help Marguerite reforge the covenant at the Standing Stones before the solstice, when the wild realm's slow death will spill into the human world. In the end Felix sacrifices his hidden, careful life — and his ability to lie to himself — choosing truth and loyalty over the safety of silence, and the covenant is renewed at a cost neither of them expected.
about_author: Oscar Montrose is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing extinct languages before turning to fiction. He writes fantasy about people who hear too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Impossible Things
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. He balances the Ledgerhouse's accounts of impossible trades while secretly listening to the rats in the walls, who gossip about a 'hollowing' in the wild. Establishes his double life and quiet loneliness. Emotional beat: wary contentment built on concealment.

chapters.title: A Knock Before Dawn
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A half-dead woman leaves a child at the guild's door and vanishes; the child speaks a language no clerk recognizes. Felix alone hears the beasts outside answering her. Emotional beat: dread and reluctant fascination.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Spoke First
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Marguerite, feral and untrusting, is locked in the counting room while the guild debates what she's worth. Felix slips her food and hears her speak to the moths. Emotional beat: tenderness he can't afford.

chapters.title: What the Rats Remember
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The cellar rats describe a broken promise made 'when the stones went quiet,' hinting the guild caused it. Felix begins searching the archives. Emotional beat: the first crack in his loyalty to the guild.

chapters.title: The Undercroft Archive
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In sealed ledgers he finds the Old Covenant's terms and a page torn out — signed by the Ledgermaster himself. He hides the book in his coat. Emotional beat: vertigo of discovery.

chapters.title: Marguerite
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV, her language rendered strange and lovely. She names herself, remembers her mother's flight, and judges Felix by how the beasts trust him. Emotional beat: grief braided with fierce curiosity.

chapters.title: The Ledgermaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The Ledgermaster, Aldous Vane, questions Felix gently, too gently, about the child and the missing page. Felix lies for the first time to the guild. Emotional beat: terror of being seen.

chapters.title: A Price on Small Heads
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vane posts a quiet bounty; the enforcer Sable Harrow takes the contract. Marguerite overhears the clerks and understands she is merchandise. Emotional beat: cold clarity.

chapters.title: The Night of Broken Locks
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix frees Marguerite through the coal chute; the stable horses cover their escape with screams only he can hear. Emotional beat: the point of no return.

chapters.title: Out of the City's Teeth
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They flee through the docklands; Felix bargains with gull-flocks and a one-eyed cat who knows the wild roads. Emotional beat: exhilaration shadowed by guilt.

chapters.title: Sable Harrow
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. The enforcer tracks them, revealing her own history: she once heard the beasts too, and the guild cut it out of her. Emotional beat: wounded menace, almost pity.

chapters.title: The Green Road
chapters.summary: Felix and Marguerite's POVs. They enter the overgrown wild road; Marguerite teaches Felix the old tongue's first words. Emotional beat: fragile partnership becoming friendship.

chapters.title: The Hollowing
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She shows Felix a forest going grey and silent — the wild realm dying where the covenant broke. Felix hears nothing at all, and it terrifies him. Emotional beat: awe curdling into urgency.

chapters.title: The Fox with a Debt
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A fox who owes Felix's grandmother a favor becomes their guide and comic relief, but warns that the Standing Stones demand payment. Emotional beat: warmth with an undertow.

chapters.title: What Felix's Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Felix's POV, with flashback. He realizes his grandmother's 'bird stories' were covenant-keeping; his gift is inheritance, not accident. Emotional beat: identity remade.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Toll
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. A river spirit demands a memory as passage; Marguerite pays one of her mother, and Felix lies to spare her the worst of it. Emotional beat: sacrifice and its first cost.

chapters.title: Vane's Ledger
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Flashback: thirty years ago, Vane broke the covenant to corner the trade in impossible things, believing order required the wild's taming. Emotional beat: chilling self-justification.

chapters.title: The Village of Quiet Bells
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. A village where no one dreams anymore shelters them for a night; a dying elder blesses Marguerite as 'the last word of the first tongue.' Emotional beat: the stakes made human.

chapters.title: Caught
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable corners them at a ford; Marguerite speaks to her in the old tongue, and Sable's severed gift aches awake. She lets them go — for now. Emotional beat: mercy as rebellion.

chapters.title: The Turning of the Fox
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The fox is captured by guild hunters and, tortured, reveals their route. Felix's guilt becomes resolve. Emotional beat: fury and grief.

chapters.title: The Guild's Long Arm
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vane dispatches the full hunt and seals the city; allies who helped Felix are arrested. Emotional beat: the net closing.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Doubt
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She learns the covenant requires a willing heir to be 'unmade and remade' at the Stones — she may not survive it. She considers running. Emotional beat: fear of the price.

chapters.title: The Confession at the Fire
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix confesses he lied at the river to spare her; Marguerite's trust shatters and slowly re-forms. Emotional beat: loyalty tested by truth — the theme made flesh.

chapters.title: The Standing Stones
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. They reach the Stones at last, grey and dumb, and read the covenant's full terms carved in the first tongue. Emotional beat: solemnity.

chapters.title: Sable's Choice
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Ordered to take them alive, Sable instead burns her guild seal and stands with them, her half-remembered gift returning in fragments. Emotional beat: redemption earned.

chapters.title: Vane Arrives
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Vane's column surrounds the Stones with iron and ledgers, intending a 'managed' covenant the guild controls. Emotional beat: dread before the storm.

chapters.title: The Terms of the Bargain
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Vane offers Felix everything he ever wanted — legitimacy, safety, the gift made lawful — if he delivers Marguerite. Emotional beat: temptation at its most seductive.

chapters.title: The Refusal
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix refuses publicly, declaring the truth of the broken covenant to hunters and beasts alike; his hidden life ends in a single sentence. Emotional beat: liberation through ruin.

chapters.title: The Battle of the Stones
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Beasts answer Felix's call; Sable holds the line; the fox, escaped, turns the flank. Emotional beat: desperate, costly courage.

chapters.title: Vane's Fall
chapters.summary: Vane's POV. Confronted by the dying wild he caused, Vane clings to his ledger until the Stones themselves render judgment — he is unmade into ink and ash. Emotional beat: tragic, earned downfall.

chapters.title: The Remaking
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Marguerite steps into the covenant's fire, speaks the first tongue whole, and is unmade and remade — no longer only a child, but a voice between realms. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into purpose.

chapters.title: What Felix Gave
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The renewed covenant demands a speaker's bond; Felix offers his gift freely, and the beasts give it back changed — he now hears the wild realm itself, and it is overwhelming. Emotional beat: sacrifice rewarded at a price.

chapters.title: The Grey Receding
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Color and sound return to the hollowed forest; the ferryman returns Marguerite's mother's memory as a gift. Emotional beat: quiet, disbelieving joy.

chapters.title: After the Fire
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. The guild lies broken; survivors look to Felix and Sable, who want only rest. The fox collects its debt with a wink and vanishes. Emotional beat: exhaustion and peace.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix reopens the Ledgerhouse as something honest — a house of exchange between realms, with Marguerite as its voice. Emotional beat: rebuilding with open eyes.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Name
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. She chooses what her name means now, and asks Felix to teach her human words the way she taught him old ones. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not given.

chapters.title: Letters to the Dead
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. Felix visits his grandmother's grave and finally reads her bird stories aloud, understanding them fully for the first time. Emotional beat: grief resolved into gratitude.

chapters.title: The Solstice Bell
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. One year later, the covenant is renewed publicly at the Stones; the village bells ring loud again. Sable departs to find others like her. Emotional beat: hard-won harmony.

chapters.title: The Voice in the Walls
chapters.summary: Felix's POV. In the Ledgerhouse cellar, the rats tell Felix of a door in the far north that the old covenant sealed — and it has begun to rattle. Emotional beat: peace shadowed by wonder.

chapters.title: Marguerite and the Crown
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Marguerite is offered the wild realm's crown and accepts not as ruler but as promise-keeper; Felix stands beside her as its witness. The door in the north waits. Emotional beat: triumphant, open-ended close.
